title: How Data Science is Changing Everything
description: A talk by Chloe Nelson exploring the frontiers of data science. Filmed at TED Salon.
tags: data_science, brain, future of work, virtual reality
transcript: Thank you. I want to talk about Data Science. For the past 13 years, I have been studying Data Science and its impact on our world. What we found is remarkable. Data Science is fundamentally changing the way we think about behavioral neuroscience. Let me share three key insights. First, social connections are the strongest predictor of long-term happiness. Second, human collaboration amplifies individual effort tenfold. Third, most decisions are made emotionally and justified rationally afterwards. Let me give you a concrete example. In our lab, we tested this idea with students across 12 universities. The results were striking. Those who adopted the new approach showed a 40% improvement in outcomes. This tells us something profound about Data Science. When we look at the broader picture, we see that early education interventions yield lifelong returns. And this is not just theory. Real world applications are already emerging. Companies and institutions are starting to adopt these principles. The implications for behavioral neuroscience are enormous. If we embrace these ideas, we can build a better future. But it requires courage, collaboration, and a willingness to change. So I ask you today: what role will you play in shaping the future of Data Science? Thank you.

Working in neural networks, I began to notice patterns that did not fit the conventional wisdom. early education interventions yield lifelong returns. So my team and I decided to dig deeper. We collected data from patients in a clinical trial. The results were consistent across age groups, genders, and backgrounds. What we found changed my perspective entirely. data-driven decisions consistently outperform intuition. And it gets more interesting. social connections are the strongest predictor of long-term happiness. When we shared our results, some people were skeptical. That is fair. But the evidence is compelling. micro-habits compound into macro-level change over time. I believe we are standing at the beginning of a revolution in Law. Not a violent one, but a revolution of ideas. The kind that reshapes how we see the world and our place in it. So I leave you with this thought: the future of Law is not written. It is being written right now, by people like you. Thank you.

title: Why Climate Matters More Than Ever
description: A talk by Iris Quinn exploring the frontiers of climate. Filmed at TED2015.
tags: brain, biodiversity, tedx, climate, philosophy, data
transcript: I grew up fascinated by Climate. As a researcher in climate policy, I have seen first-hand how micro-habits compound into macro-level change over time. Over 18 years of work, my team discovered that decentralised networks are more resilient than centralised ones. This has profound implications. diversity in teams produces more creative solutions. Let me walk you through what we found. We worked with a group of 500 volunteers over a period of several months. The results were consistent across age groups, genders, and backgrounds. What surprised us most was empathy is a trainable skill with measurable outcomes. It challenges everything we thought we knew about Climate. We published our findings and the response was overwhelming. Researchers from 22 countries reached out to collaborate. Together, we are now building a global network focused on Climate. The future is not something we wait for. It is something we create. We must act now to shape the future of Climate. Thank you for listening.
